contexts.text: Hence a thick darkness, or stupor and ignorance of all things of faith...
Their phantasies and persuasions induce so great a stupor on other Spirits that they do not know whether they are alive or dead.
Being penetrated with the amazement of wonder...
He said that he could not, for amazement, describe the glory of the Word...
When such approach Heaven... their mind is turned into stupor.
On hearing that they are being buried, they are smitten with a kind of stupor.

Torment = stupor, which their Persuasive induces on the understanding, as a scorpion does on the body... In the Spiritual World there exists a Persuasive which takes away the understanding of truth, and induces a stupor, and thus a pain, on the lower mind.
I was once in amazement at the vast multitude who ascribe creation to nature. CL 380:2.
The prince who shall be clothed with stupor () = inservient truth.
